title: Tool-call diff + schema-drift detector for safe model rollouts
creator: Sofia Kim
description:
Background: As we increase use of structured outputs and function/tool-calling across customer workloads, even small changes in model behavior can break downstream tooling. Existing rollout controls focus on latency/error rates and token-level diffs; we need an automated detector that verifies compatibility of structured outputs and function calls during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts and triggers safe fallback/auto-rollback when regressions are detected.

Goal: Implement a runtime-compatible tooling layer that: 1) validates model responses against a supplied JSON schema and function-call contract, 2) computes lightweight function-call diffs and a schema-drift score, 3) surfaces per-route compatibility metrics in the Console, and 4) plugs into existing rollout policies (canary/A-B/shadow) to pause or rollback when thresholds are exceeded.

Scope (this ticket):
- Design and implement an in-path "compatibility detector" that can run in parallel with normal inference (shadow mode) and as a gating check in canaries.
- Provide a compact, time-bounded schema validator optimized for common patterns (nullable fields, unions, typed arrays) with performance budgets to avoid SLO impact.
- Implement a function-call diff estimator: compares callee name, argument keys, basic argument types, and presence/absence of optional arguments; computes a numeric compatibility score.
- Expose metrics and alerts to Console rollouts: compatibility_score, schema_errors_pct, function_diff_rate, and per-field error examples.
- Hook detector outputs into rollout policies: configurable thresholds for pause/rollback, and an automatic rollback runbook.

Out of scope for this ticket: full semantic equivalence checks, heavy-weight AST diffs of nested arguments, and UI polish beyond basic Console widgets.
acceptance_criteria: Detector runs in shadow mode during a rollout and produces compatibility metrics for every request without increasing p99 latency by >10% on the canary path
Schema validator flags structural violations and returns machine-readable error types (missing_field, type_mismatch, extra_field)
Function-call diff calculates a normalized score in [0,100] and flags dropped/renamed function calls and redacted argument changes
Console shows per-route compatibility_score and an anomaly timeline; alerts are triggered when schema_errors_pct > 2% or function_diff_rate > 5% over a 5-minute window
Automated rollback is triggered when configured thresholds hit for two consecutive evaluation windows and the rollback action is recorded in rollout audit logs
Unit and integration tests cover the validator and diff logic; a canary runbook doc is added and linked
steps: Design schema validator API and lightweight error taxonomy (Sofia, 2025-02-13)
Prototype function-call diff algorithm and benchmark using historic function-call logs (Alejandro, 2025-02-14)
Add detector hook into runtime request path in shadow mode; ensure non-blocking execution and bounded CPU usage (ENG runtime team)
Instrument metrics (promcounter/gauge) for compatibility_score, schema_errors_pct, function_diff_rate
Integrate metrics into Console rollouts: widget + alerting config (Console team)
Add rollout policy configuration options (pause_thresholds and auto_rollback) and implement state machine transition
Run staged canary against internal staging models and record false positive rate; tune thresholds
Documentation: runbook, examples for customers to attach schemas and function contracts
rollout_policy_proposal: Default: run detector in shadow for initial 10% traffic for 24h; if schema_errors_pct < 0.5% and function_diff_rate < 1% promote to 50% traffic. Auto-rollback: pause + evaluate if schema_errors_pct > 2% or function_diff_rate > 5% for 5m window twice. Allow per-customer overrides and a 'lenient' mode that only alerts.
comments: 2025-02-12 Sofia Kim: Created ticket after postmortem for ENG-8803 where new model variant broke a downstream enrichment tool. Initial spec attached.

2025-02-13 Alejandro Ruiz: Prototype for schema validator implemented; using json-schema-lite with custom nullable/union handling. Initial microbench shows ~0.6ms p50 per-check in Node. Need Go runtime port for low-latency routes.
2025-02-15 Maya Patel (Console): We'll need a compact time-series and sample explorer to surface failing examples without exposing PII. Adding placeholder for sampled payload redaction.

2025-02-17 Jared O'Neill (SRE): Shadow execution must be CPU-budgeted and isolated; suggest a per-route worker pool with soft limits. Also recommended store-only-ids for high-volume routes to reduce index size.

2025-02-19 Alejandro Ruiz: Implemented function-call diff prototype and tested against two months of function logs. Found three common drift patterns: renamed optional arg, type widening (int->string), and omitted context param. Working on normalized scoring to penalize breaking changes more heavily.
2025-02-20 Sofia Kim: Set tentative thresholds in acceptance criteria based on pilot results. Scheduling a design review with PM and SRE on 2025-02-21.
